chunks: Aban narrated from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī al-Ḥalabī and Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, from ʿUbaydullāh ibn ʿAlī al-Ḥalabī, who said:
I heard Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام say:
Whatever may be of differing food, goods, or any of the things that vary in value, there is no harm in selling it two-for-one, hand-to-hand. But as for deferment, then it is not valid.

key_terms.لَا يَصْلُحُ: it is not proper or legally acceptable
key_terms.نَظِرَةً: deferment or credit-based delay in payment/delivery
key_terms.يَتَفَاضَلُ: that differ in amount or value
key_terms.يَدًا بِيَدٍ: spot exchange conducted hand-to-hand without delay

ai.seo_question: When is it permissible to exchange different goods in unequal amounts in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding exchange transactions involving items that differ in kind or value. It permits unequal exchange when the transaction is hand-to-hand, but prohibits it when there is deferment, reflecting the jurisprudential treatment of riba-related sales.
